references.text: Shortly before this testimony, John the Baptist says that he saw the Spirit descend like a dove from heaven and remain on Jesus ([ref:Joh 1:32|John 1:32]). It is this vision that forms the basis of his testimony in verse 34.

Isaiah describes the Lord's chosen servant: "Behold, my servant whom I uphold, my chosen one in whom my soul delights" ([ref:Jes 42:1|Isaiah 42:1]). The designation "God's Chosen" (ὁ ἐκλεκτὸς τοῦ θεοῦ) in John 1:34 links Jesus to this prophecy about the Lord's chosen servant.

Just before this testimony, John the Baptist points to Jesus as "the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world" ([ref:Joh 1:29|John 1:29]). Together with the declaration in verse 34, this forms a complete testimony about who Jesus is.

At the transfiguration on the mountain, a voice from the cloud says: "This is my Son, the Chosen One" (ὁ ἐκλελεγμένος) ([ref:Luk 9:35|Luke 9:35]). This divine declaration confirms the same testimony that John the Baptist gives in John 1:34.

At the cross, the leaders mock Jesus and say: "He saved others; let him save himself if he is the Christ of God, the Chosen One" ([ref:Luk 23:35|Luke 23:35]). The title "the Chosen One" is also used here for Jesus, in ironic contrast to John the Baptist's confession of faith.

At Jesus' baptism, a voice from heaven says: "This is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased" ([ref:Matt 3:17|Matthew 3:17]). This divine declaration takes place in the same context as John the Baptist's testimony and links Jesus' identity to Isaiah's servant prophecies.
Peter calls Jesus "the living stone, rejected by men but chosen and precious in God's sight" ([ref:1 Pet 2:4|1 Peter 2:4]). Here the same basic idea of Jesus as God's Chosen One is used.

"You are my witnesses," says the Lord, "and my servant whom I have chosen" ([ref:Jes 43:10|Isaiah 43:10]). The motif of God's chosen servant and testimony about him already appears in Isaiah and is fulfilled in John the Baptist's testimony.

"We have seen and testify that the Father has sent his Son as the Savior of the world" ([ref:1 Joh 4:14|1 John 4:14]). The structure "we have seen and we testify" reflects John the Baptist's "I have seen and I have testified" in John 1:34.
